body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 4f0260f50bd73c9e98e31d6e7c2050eb8c9538b8 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge. The local review found no blocking item.

Scope checked:
- I read the complete diff and issue #3379, including its comments.
- I checked the laws in current upstream main at `707dac12a85f9744640ef2f682fd5653f1fa83b9`.
- All six guards come before device creation. They remain held until the local GPU objects drop.
- The snapshot tests take the GPU lock before the snapshot lock. Existing evidence tests use the same order.
- The five tests without a GPU guard return before device creation.
- Both source pins passed. The decision file states the resource, lock order, alternatives, and limits.
- This change affects test code only. It changes no visible UI, so before/after screenshots do not apply.
- This is not a safety-tier change. It changes no G-code, collision check, gouge check, stock simulation, or geometry.

Local results:

Worktree: `.claude/worktrees/review-3972`. Its HEAD is the PR head. Upstream main is its direct parent. The trial merge reported `Already up to date.` Thus, no merge commit was needed, and `HEAD^1` is the base SHA, not the PR SHA.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | PASS: 11 steps; 0 failed; 0 stalled |
| UI build, selected targets, `--no-run` | PASS |
| UI lib, 16 test threads | PASS: 1646 passed; 8 ignored |
| `boundary` | PASS: 3 passed |
| `boundary_picks` | PASS: 7 passed |
| `contour_dxf_sketch` | PASS: 2 passed |
| `egui_app`, 16 test threads | PASS: 8 passed |
| `sinker_setup` | PASS: 2 passed |
| `tap_hand` | PASS: 3 passed |
| `theme_example` | PASS: 3 passed |
| `theme_files` | PASS: 17 passed |
| `waterjet_tool` | PASS: 1 passed |
| `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | PASS |
| `cargo xtask gate light` | PASS: 6 steps; 11 tests passed; 0 failed; 0 stalled |
| `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` | PASS |

The UI suites ran from `crates/ui`. Both named lock pins passed in the lib suite. The light tests were `motion` lib (7), `adaptive_troch_island` (1), `adaptive_troch_neck` (1), `adaptive_troch_parallel` (1), and app `pocket_pass_start` (1).

Extra suites run: the five light suites listed above. No changed fixture or importer requires another suite. The diff does not require catalog tests.

Mutations: not run. This change is outside the safety tier. I did not change the code. The author's six red/green mutation results were not independently repeated.

Goldens moved: none. The diff changes no recorded program or snapshot PNG. I did not run the ignored pixel tests or full heavy lanes.

Requested before merge: none from this review.

Notes:
- These local results are from Linux. They do not prove that the Windows crash has stopped.
- The PR body asks the merging session to wait for the separate Windows results from `lenny` and `bacon`. Those results are not present in this review.
- The worktree and branch remain in place to keep the build cache warm. No GitHub runner was used.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Left for the maintainer: the only `pr-reviewer` marker at head `4f0260f` is authored by the PR author (mkinney) and never counts, and the Windows crash repro results from `lenny` and `bacon` (named in the PR body as a precondition) are not present. No clean counted review at the current head.

Windows repro on lenny (the desktop that showed the crash), head `4f0260f50`. Three runs of each, 12 test threads:

| Run | `camcraft-ui --lib` | `--test egui_app` |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1647 passed, 0 failed (74 s) | 8 passed |
| 2 | 1647 passed, 0 failed (80 s) | 8 passed |
| 3 | 1647 passed, 0 failed (76 s) | 8 passed |

No `0xC0000005` / `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION`. The crash was intermittent before, so this is good evidence, not proof. Bacon's next main check after merge gives a second Windows machine.

Update to my earlier note: the lenny repro is now present and green. Three runs, 12 test threads each, no `0xC0000005`/STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION: `camcraft-ui --lib` 1647 passed (74 s / 80 s / 76 s) and `--test egui_app` 8 passed (three runs). The crash was intermittent before, so this is good evidence, not proof. Bacon's next main check after merge gives the second Windows machine. The PR still has no counted clean review at the head (only the author's own marker), so it stays for the maintainer to approve and merge by hand.

Label: `needs-rework` (removed `merge-ready`). The code review is clean and green locally, but one blocker remains: the Windows crash reproduction that the PR body names as a merge precondition (#3379) is not present at head `4f0260f`. CI/draft state is left as the contributor set it (fork PR).
